proposals.before: A Huainan West circuit military commissioner was appointed, commanding five commanderies—Yiyang, Yiyang, Yingchuan, Xingyang, and Runan—from his seat at Yingchuan.
proposals.after: A Huainan West circuit military commissioner was appointed, commanding five commanderies—Yiyang (義陽), Yiyang (弋陽), Yingchuan, Xingyang, and Runan—from his seat at Yingchuan.
proposals.reason: Chinese lists 義陽 then 弋陽 as two different commanderies; both were romanized identically as Yiyang, obscuring that they are distinct places.

proposals.before: The Huainan West circuit military commissioner was established, holding Yiyang, Yiyang, Yingchuan, Xingyang, and Runan commanderies—five in all—with seat at Yingchuan commandery.
proposals.after: The Huainan West circuit military commissioner was established, holding Yiyang (義陽), Yiyang (弋陽), Yingchuan, Xingyang, and Runan commanderies—five in all—with seat at Yingchuan commandery.
proposals.reason: Literal English also collapses 義陽 and 弋陽 into the same spelling without distinguishing the two commanderies named in the Chinese.

proposals.before: In 759, the second year of Zhide, the Bianzhou chief defense commissioner was abolished and replaced by a Bian–Hua military commissioner at Hua Prefecture, commanding Hua, Pu, Bian, Cao, and Song.
proposals.after: In 759, the second year of Qianyuan, the Bianzhou chief defense commissioner was abolished and replaced by a Bian–Hua military commissioner at Hua Prefecture, commanding Hua, Pu, Bian, Cao, and Song.
proposals.reason: After 乾元元年 in the prior unit, 759 二年 is Qianyuan year 2; Zhide ended in 757, so calling 759 a Zhide year is wrong.

proposals.before: Pinglu Army military commissioner Hou Xiy led his troops to hold Qingzhou and was appointed Qing–Mi military commissioner; the Zi–Yi circuit was then abolished and its five prefectures absorbed into the newly styled Zi–Qing–Pinglu circuit, which also gained Qi Prefecture.
proposals.after: Pinglu Army military commissioner Hou Xiyi led his troops to hold Qingzhou and was appointed Qing–Mi military commissioner; the Zi–Yi circuit was then abolished and its five prefectures absorbed into the newly styled Zi–Qing–Pinglu circuit, which also gained Qi Prefecture.
proposals.reason: Chinese 侯希逸 is Hou Xiyi; the idiomatic spelling truncates the given name to Xiy.

proposals.before: The Pinglu Army military commissioner Hou Xiy led troops to hold Qingzhou; he was appointed Qing-Mi military commissioner, whereupon the Zi-Yi circuit was abolished and its five prefectures were merged in, styled the Zi-Qing-Pinglu circuit, and Qi Prefecture was added to its jurisdiction.
proposals.after: The Pinglu Army military commissioner Hou Xiyi led troops to hold Qingzhou; he was appointed Qing-Mi military commissioner, whereupon the Zi-Yi circuit was abolished and its five prefectures were merged in, styled the Zi-Qing-Pinglu circuit, and Qi Prefecture was added to its jurisdiction.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise truncates 希逸 to Xiy instead of Xiyi.
